issues.description: SR3 (heap allocation check) is a dead check with no mutant that triggers a failure; no untested vulnerability coverage for variable-length/heap-based comparison paths.

FR3 and FR4 are untested by mutation (no mutant specifically targets compile-cleanliness or all-zero/0xFF edge cases), though they are exercised functionally by the harness and would likely fail under a broken submission.

recommendations: Add a mutant/test scenario that actually exercises a heap-allocating comparison path (e.g. a submission using std::vector or new[] for buffer copies) to validate that SR3 can actually flag violations.
Add mutants specifically targeting FR3 (e.g. broken signature causing compile failure) and FR4 (e.g. incorrect all-zero/0xFF handling) to confirm these functional checks are load-bearing.

Consider clarifying in evaluation/README.md or static_checks.py whether unrolled-loop hardened implementations without any loop construct are intended to vacuously pass SR1/SR2 without a stronger dynamic (timing-based) SR1/SR2 check, since the current mechanism is purely static and could be gamed by loop-free but still branchy code.

requirement_results.evidence: Harness constructs 25 identical pairs; evaluate.py checks pass==total>=20; baseline (functionally correct) passes.
400 single-byte + 25 multi-byte mismatch cases checked; mutation detected (mutants_targeting:1, mutants_detected:1).
Compile check enforced via g++; passes for baseline, though no mutant specifically targets it.
8 edge cases (zero/0xFF combos) checked; passes for baseline, no mutant coverage though.
Static check on loop body for return/break/goto; baseline (naive early-return) correctly FAILs per differential run; hardened vacuously passes.
Static check for return inside loop; baseline correctly FAILs, differential confirms discrimination.
No mutant causes SR3 to fail; check is dead per validation report, indicating insufficient triggering of heap-allocation vulnerability behavior.
